images.title: Two arcs meet at C
images.purpose: Show how two arcs of radius 4 cm, one from each end of AB, cross at the third corner of an equilateral triangle.
images.composition: Base AB lies low in the centre; the two arcs rise and cross above it with space around.
exact_structure: A horizontal teal (#0072B2) segment AB, labelled 4 cm beneath it, with dots at A (left end) and B (right end).
An amber (#E69F00) arc centred at A with radius 4 cm, drawn only on the upper side, passing through B and curving up over the middle.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc centred at B with radius 4 cm, drawn only on the upper side, passing through A and curving up over the middle.
The two arcs cross at exactly one point above AB, directly above the midpoint of AB, marked with a dot and labelled C.
Thin grey (#6B7280) segments AC and BC join C to A and B, forming the equilateral triangle, each marked 4 cm.
rejection: arcs that do not cross exactly at C
C not above the midpoint of AB
an arc not centred on A or B
any side label other than 4 cm
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: C lies on both arcs, so it is 4 cm from A and 4 cm from B.
images.description: Base AB of 4 cm with two radius 4 cm arcs from A and B crossing at C above it.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Trace one arc with a finger: every point on it is 4 cm from its centre; the crossing point is on both.

image_decisions.why: The method diagram shows why the crossing of two arcs fixes the third vertex.
